title: Clear Aligner Cost
meta_title: Clear Aligner Cost: What Affects It | West Alexandria Dental Care
meta_description: What affects the cost of clear aligner treatment: complexity, length, refinements and retainers. How orthodontic insurance benefits and lifetime maximums.
h1: What affects the cost of clear aligners
intro: Aligner treatment is priced by the case, not by the tray. A few months of minor straightening and eighteen months of bite correction are different undertakings, and the cost reflects that. Here is what drives the number, how insurance tends to help, and why you get the figure in writing at the consultation rather than from a price list.

items.title: Complexity
items.body: Minor crowding or spacing needs few trays and little chair time. Bite correction, rotations and large movements need many more trays, attachments and more supervision.

items.title: Length of treatment
items.body: More months means more check-ins and, often, more trays. Treatment that runs long because of poor wear can also add refinement sets.

items.title: Refinements
items.body: A short extra series to finish teeth that lag the plan. Common and usually included; ask so you know.

items.title: Retainers
items.body: Made at the end and essential. Confirm whether they are included and what replacements cost.

items.title: Preparatory work
items.body: Gum treatment or fillings needed before teeth are moved are priced separately, because they are needed regardless.

items.title: One or both arches
items.body: Treating only the upper or only the lower is sometimes possible and costs less, though the bite often needs both.

sections.heading: How orthodontic insurance works
body: Many dental plans include an orthodontic benefit, usually a lifetime maximum per person rather than an annual one, paid as a percentage of the fee up to that maximum. Some plans limit it to children under a certain age; some include adults. The benefit is typically paid over the course of treatment rather than all at once. Aligners are generally covered the same way as braces.

We accept Aetna, Ameritas, Delta Dental, Humana, Cigna, MetLife and Virginia Medicaid, and we check your orthodontic benefit before the consultation ends so the written estimate shows your actual out-of-pocket cost. Virginia Medicaid covers orthodontics for children only in limited, medically necessary cases, and we tell you if yours qualifies. See [understanding dental insurance](/new-patients/understanding-dental-insurance/) for the terms.

items.title: Consultation
items.body: Exam, records and a discussion of what you want. We determine the complexity and whether aligners suit the case.

items.title: Benefits checked
items.body: Your orthodontic coverage, lifetime maximum, age limits and how the plan pays are confirmed with your insurer.

items.title: Written estimate
items.body: The full fee, what it includes, your expected insurance contribution and your out-of-pocket cost, in writing. No obligation.

items.title: Payment options
items.body: Ask when you call about ways to spread the cost over treatment. The office will tell you what is available.

sections.heading: Why we do not publish a price
sections.body: A single figure would be wrong for most people, too high for simple cases and too low for complex ones, and it would encourage choosing treatment by price rather than suitability. The consultation gives you a real number for your own teeth, and the digital plan shows what that number buys.

faqs.a: Usually, and that is the point of them. The trade-off is no in-person examination, no X-rays, no check that the gums and bone are healthy, no attachments for difficult movements and no one adjusting the plan when teeth do not track. For simple spacing they may work; for anything else the savings often turn into a correction later.
Ask at the consultation; the written estimate states what is included. Retainers are essential and we make sure you know their cost up front, including replacements over the years.

faqs.q: Can I use a flexible spending or health savings account?
faqs.a: Orthodontic treatment is generally an eligible expense for FSA and HSA accounts. Check your plan's rules; the office can provide the documentation you need.

faqs.q: What if treatment takes longer than planned?
faqs.a: The estimate is for the planned treatment including normal refinements. Treatment that runs long because trays were not worn may add cost, which is one more reason the wear commitment matters.

cta.heading: Your number, for your teeth, in writing.
cta.body: Book a consultation. You leave with the digital plan, the timeline and a written estimate with your insurance already checked.
